text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests evaluated against established glucose and A1C thresholds.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests evaluated against established glucose and A1C thresholds

text_blocks.snippet: According to guidelines from the American Diabetes Association, a diagnosis requires meeting at least one of the following criteria (ideally confirmed by a repeat test on a second day, unless classic symptoms are present):

list.snippet: A1C Test: Measures average blood sugar over the past 2 to 3 months. No fasting is required.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures blood sugar after an 8-hour overnight fast.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures blood sugar 2 hours after drinking a sugary liquid during a 75-gram glucose test.
Random Plasma Glucose Test: Checked at any time of day when severe symptoms of high blood sugar are present.
Diabetes threshold: 200 mg/dL or higher alongside symptoms (like extreme thirst, frequent urination, or unexplained weight loss).

text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes develops slowly, and some people have no symptoms at first. Common signs include:

list.snippet: Tingling or numbness in the hands or feet
